Guides

Why is my home Wi-Fi so slow? 7 common causes

If your Wi-Fi drags, you are not alone. Most slow Wi-Fi comes from a small number of causes, and several are easy to check yourself.

1. The router is in a bad spot. Routers on the floor, inside a cabinet or in a basement corner struggle. Wi-Fi works best out in the open and up high, near the middle of your home.

2. Too far, too many walls. Brick, concrete and metal weaken the signal. If one room is poor, distance and walls are likely the reason.

3. An old router. Routers do wear out and fall behind. If yours is many years old, newer models handle more devices at once.

4. Too many devices. Phones, TVs, tablets, cameras and speakers all share the connection. Busy homes need better equipment than quiet ones.

5. Interference. Neighbours' networks, microwaves and cordless phones can crowd the same channels.

6. A slow plan or a busy time. Test your speed next to the router. If it is slow even there, the issue may be your internet plan or provider, not your home network.

7. Out-of-date settings or software. Routers need occasional updates, and a restart sometimes clears a stuck connection.

What to try first. Restart the router, move it to a central open spot, and test your speed in the room where it is bad. If that does not help, a short visit to test coverage and adjust or add equipment usually solves it.
